title: Matomo vs Google Analytics
description: Matomo vs Google Analytics 4 — compare GA4 consent and cookies, data ownership, Cloud vs self-hosted Matomo cost, and when a simpler hosted option like Fathom is enough.
verdict: Choose Matomo when you need GA4-like web reporting with data you own, EU Cloud hosting in Frankfurt, or a self-hosted install. Choose Google Analytics 4 when Google Ads, Search Console, BigQuery, and a $0 standard-property bill matter more than where hits are processed.
quickAnswer: This page answers **Matomo vs Google Analytics** and **Matomo vs Google Analytics 4**. **Matomo** is the better fit if data ownership, EU hosting, or self-hosting matter — Cloud or On-Premise, without sending hits to Google. **Google Analytics 4** is the better fit if you need free scale and deep Google Ads / Search Console / BigQuery workflows and can accept Google as the processor. Universal Analytics is shut down; this comparison is GA4 only.
bottomLine: Matomo vs Google Analytics 4 is the same reporting job under two trust models. Matomo wins when legal, residency, or ownership rules out Google. GA4 wins when the Google ads stack and a $0 standard tier outweigh those constraints. If you only need traffic stats without running Matomo or learning GA4, [Fathom](/tools/fathom/) is a simpler hosted option — see [Matomo vs Fathom](/compare/fathom-vs-matomo/).

faq.question: Matomo vs Google Analytics 4?
faq.answer: Pick Matomo if you need data ownership, Frankfurt Cloud hosting or self-hosting, and GA-like web reports (goals, ecommerce, funnels). Pick Google Analytics 4 if you need native Google Ads / Search Console / BigQuery workflows and a free standard property. This is Matomo vs Google Analytics 4, not Universal Analytics — UA standard properties stopped processing on 1 July 2023 ([Google](https://support.google.com/analytics/answer/11583528), checked 2026-11-24).

faq.question: Is Universal Analytics still part of this comparison?
faq.answer: No. Google Analytics 4 replaced Universal Analytics. Standard UA properties stopped processing data on 1 July 2023; remaining UA interface and API access ended around 1 July 2024 ([Google](https://support.google.com/analytics/answer/11583528), checked 2026-11-24). New measurement belongs in a GA4 property or in Matomo — not in a Universal Analytics property.

faq.question: Does Matomo avoid cookie consent banners like GA4 requires?
faq.answer: Not by default. Google’s own consent guide says you need to ask website visitors for consent so the Google tag can write and read cookies, then pass Consent Mode signals ([Obtain user consent](https://support.google.com/analytics/answer/14009343), [Consent Mode](https://developers.google.com/tag-platform/security/guides/consent), checked 2026-11-24). Matomo can be configured with IP anonymization, cookieless tracking, opt-out, and no PII ([Matomo privacy](https://matomo.org/privacy/), checked 2026-11-24). France’s CNIL says audience-measurement cookies can be exempt from consent only when they are strictly limited to anonymous stats for the site owner and do not enable cross-site tracking or sharing non-anonymous data with third parties ([CNIL](https://www.cnil.fr/fr/cookies-solutions-pour-les-outils-de-mesure-daudience), checked 2026-11-24). Heatmaps, session recording, ecommerce, and User-ID typically need a different legal basis — get counsel for your setup.

faq.question: Who owns the data in Matomo vs Google Analytics 4?
faq.answer: Matomo states that Cloud and On-Premise both give 100% data ownership; Cloud stores data in Frankfurt, Germany, and On-Premise lets you choose the server location ([Matomo pricing](https://matomo.org/pricing/), checked 2026-11-24). GA4 processes hits on Google infrastructure. Google Analytics customers can accept Google Ads Data Processing Terms in account settings ([Data Processing Terms](https://support.google.com/analytics/answer/3379636), checked 2026-11-24). You remain the controller; Google is still the processor, and hits leave your servers.

faq.question: How much does Matomo Cloud cost vs self-hosted Matomo vs GA4?
faq.answer: Standard GA4 has no subscription fee; Google Analytics 360 is a custom contract with no public list price (see [Google Analytics cost](/learn/google-analytics-cost/)). Matomo Cloud starts at €22/month excl. tax for 50,000 hits (USD $26 in the same JSON-LD) and includes hosting, maintenance, automatic updates, security monitoring, daily backups, and Cloud features; data is stored in Frankfurt ([Matomo pricing](https://matomo.org/pricing/), checked 2026-11-24). On-Premise Community core is free (unlimited users and hits); you pay for the server, SSL, backups, and ops. Paid On-Premise bundles start at €230/month (Team), €1,209/month (Business), and €2,834/month (Enterprise) on that same pricing page (checked 2026-11-24). Server SKU prices are not published by Matomo — see [self-hosted web analytics](/learn/self-hosted-web-analytics/).

faq.question: Is Matomo a drop-in replacement for Google Analytics 4?
faq.answer: For many marketing and ecommerce reports (goals, ecommerce, custom dimensions, funnels), Matomo Cloud includes those features in the hosted plans ([Matomo pricing](https://matomo.org/pricing/), checked 2026-11-24). It does not match GA4’s Google Ads linking, Consent Mode ads signals, or BigQuery export path ([BigQuery export](https://support.google.com/analytics/answer/9358801), checked 2026-11-24). Expect new tags, goals, and no one-to-one metric match with old Universal Analytics dashboards.

faq.question: When should I pick Fathom instead of Matomo or GA4?
faq.answer: Pick [Fathom](/tools/fathom/) when you want hosted, cookieless traffic analytics without running Matomo or learning GA4. Hosted Standard starts at $15/month for 100,000 pageviews and Fathom states no cookie banners are required for its tracking ([Fathom pricing](https://usefathom.com/pricing), checked 2026-11-24) — confirm with counsel. It is not a GA4-style suite. Head-to-head: [Matomo vs Fathom](/compare/fathom-vs-matomo/).

faq.question: Can I run GA4 and Matomo together?
faq.answer: Yes. Some teams keep GA4 for ads attribution while Matomo holds primary reporting or privacy-sensitive properties. That doubles script weight and consent work, so treat it as a bridge unless both processors are required.

editorialNotes.title: This is Matomo vs Google Analytics 4
editorialNotes.content:
Searchers still type **Matomo vs Google Analytics**. The live Google product is **Google Analytics 4**. Universal Analytics (properties whose IDs started with `UA-`) stopped processing on **1 July 2023**, and Google removed remaining UA access around **1 July 2024** ([GA4 has replaced Universal Analytics](https://support.google.com/analytics/answer/11583528), checked 2026-11-24).

GA4 is event-based (pageviews, scrolls, and purchases are events with parameters). Matomo still looks closer to classic web-analytics reports. Do not expect UA session metrics, GA4 events, and Matomo hits to match one-for-one after a migration.

editorialNotes.title: Consent and cookies
editorialNotes.content:
Google documents that when a user visits your website, you need to ask for consent so the Google tag can write and read cookies ([Obtain user consent](https://support.google.com/analytics/answer/14009343), checked 2026-11-24). For EEA traffic, Consent Mode v2 adds `ad_user_data` and `ad_personalization` on top of `ad_storage` and `analytics_storage` ([Consent Mode](https://developers.google.com/tag-platform/security/guides/consent), checked 2026-11-24). If `analytics_storage` is denied, Google says tags send cookieless pings instead of reading or writing analytics cookies.

Matomo’s default JavaScript tracker can use first-party cookies. Cookieless mode (`disableCookies()`) exists, and Matomo documents that unique-visitor and some attribution reports get less accurate without cookies ([cookieless FAQ](https://matomo.org/faq/general/faq_156/), checked 2026-11-24). Privacy controls include opt-out, IP anonymization, Do Not Track, and disabling the visits log ([Matomo privacy](https://matomo.org/privacy/), checked 2026-11-24).

CNIL’s public criteria for **consent-exempt** audience measurement: anonymous stats for the publisher only, no cross-site identifier, no sharing of non-anonymous data with third parties ([CNIL, 4 July 2025](https://www.cnil.fr/fr/cookies-solutions-pour-les-outils-de-mesure-daudience), checked 2026-11-24). CNIL also tells vendors not to call a tool “certified” or “validated by the CNIL.” A default Matomo Cloud install with heatmaps or ecommerce is not automatically exempt. Ask counsel; do not treat a logo as a legal opinion.

editorialNotes.title: Data ownership
editorialNotes.content:
Matomo’s pricing page states that **all hosting options give you 100% data ownership**. Cloud data is stored in **Frankfurt, Germany**. On-Premise lets you put the database wherever you run servers. You can migrate Cloud ↔ On-Premise because you own the data ([Matomo pricing FAQ](https://matomo.org/pricing/), checked 2026-11-24).

GA4 hits are collected by Google. You can accept the **Google Ads Data Processing Terms** in Analytics account settings ([Data Processing Terms](https://support.google.com/analytics/answer/3379636), checked 2026-11-24). That is a processor contract, not the same as hosting the database yourself. If the constraint is **where the data lives**, Matomo (especially On-Premise) is the serious alternative. If the constraint is **paid-search attribution inside Google**, GA4 remains hard to replace.

editorialNotes.title: Matomo Cloud vs self-hosted cost
editorialNotes.content:
Prices below were checked on **2026-11-24** against [Matomo pricing](https://matomo.org/pricing/) **JSON-LD** (`UnitPriceSpecification`). The HTML traffic slider can render a different default than the structured offers; we quote the JSON-LD **50,000 hits/month** Cloud offer: **€22/month excl. tax** (USD **$26**).

| | Matomo Cloud | Matomo On-Premise (self-hosted) | Google Analytics 4 |
|---|---|---|---|
| Software / SaaS | **€22/month excl. tax** (USD **$26**) at **50,000 hits** | Community core **free**; paid bundles from **€230/month** (Team), **€1,209/month** (Business), **€2,834/month** (Enterprise) | Standard property **$0**; [GA4 360](/compare/google-analytics-4-vs-google-analytics-360/) is a custom contract |
| Who hosts | Matomo | You (server, SSL, backups, upgrades) | Google |
| Data location | Frankfurt, Germany | Wherever you install it | Google infrastructure |
| Included with the fee | Hosting, maintenance, automatic updates, security monitoring, daily backups, Cloud features | Community: base analytics. Bundles add premium plugins (funnels, heatmaps, A/B tests, and others by tier) | Collection and reporting inside standard [GA4 limits](/learn/google-analytics-cost/) |
| Websites (published) | 30 on Cloud Business | Unlimited on Community | Unlimited properties on the free tier (directory snapshot) |

**Choose Cloud** if nobody wants to run PHP and a database. **Choose On-Premise** if you must pick the country or network, or if hit volume makes per-hit Cloud pricing expensive and you already have ops. Matomo does not publish a VPS SKU price; treat self-hosting as a small production service. Detail: [self-hosted web analytics](/learn/self-hosted-web-analytics/).

GA4’s invoice can still be $0 while consent banners, Tag Manager, and optional BigQuery storage/query charges add cost — see [Google Analytics cost](/learn/google-analytics-cost/).

editorialNotes.title: When Fathom is the simpler hosted option
editorialNotes.content:
Matomo is for teams that still want **serious web analytics**. If the weekly question is only which pages and channels brought traffic, a lightweight hosted product is less work than Matomo Cloud, On-Premise, or GA4.

[Fathom Analytics](/tools/fathom/) is that simpler hosted path: cookieless by design, no server to patch. [Fathom pricing](https://usefathom.com/pricing) (checked 2026-11-24) lists **Standard at $15/month** for **100,000 pageviews**, 50 sites included, same analytics features on every plan, and a 7-day trial. Fathom states **no cookie banners required**; that is the vendor’s claim, not a regulator letter — confirm with counsel. It will not replace GA4 Ads attribution or Matomo ecommerce/heatmaps.

Fair split: stay on **GA4** for Google ads; pick **Matomo** for ownership and depth; pick **Fathom** for a dashboard people will actually open. Pair-wise detail: [Matomo vs Fathom](/compare/fathom-vs-matomo/).

editorialNotes.title: Performance
editorialNotes.content: We publish recorded script benchmarks on our [benchmarks hub](/benchmarks/) — never estimated numbers. Both GA4’s default gtag install and Matomo Cloud’s default snippet are measured; self-hosted Matomo and plugin bundles can weigh differently, so compare the install you will actually ship.

alsoConsider.note: Simpler hosted analytics when you want cookieless traffic stats without Matomo ops or GA4’s consent and ads stack. Not a replacement for ecommerce depth or Google Ads attribution.
